results.title: Resurf 2
results.content:
Resurf 2 is out. It's not an update to the old app. It's a different app that happens to have the same name and the same idea. Written from scratch in Swift, running natively on Mac, iPhone and iPad, syncing between them through your own iCloud account.

Here's what changed and why.

Resurf on Mac, iPhone and iPad

## Why rewrite it

Resurf 1 was an Electron app. That got the product out of my head and onto people's machines, which was the only thing that mattered at the time. But it came with a ceiling: a slow cold start, a Dock icon that ate memory sitting still, scrolling that never felt right, and no credible path to a phone app. [...] Resurf 1 won't update itself into Resurf 2: different app, different updater. You'll need to download it.

## What's next

The coming weeks are all about polish: fixing the bugs you report and shipping the quality-of-life improvements you submit. Most of what made Resurf 1 better came straight from user messages, and Resurf 2 will work the same way: tell me what's rough, and watch it get fixed.

## Found a bug?

Resurf 2 is a brand-new codebase, and some bugs only show up in the wild, on libraries, Macs, and workflows unlike mine. If something misbehaves, report it or email support@resurf.so. Reports land directly with me, and fixes ship fast.

## Thank you [...] ## Sync that isn't a server

Your devices sync through your own iCloud account. There's no Resurf account, no login, no server holding your library. I can't see your captures because there's nowhere for me to look.

Everything still lives as plain files on your Mac: markdown notes, original images, original PDFs, in folders you can open in Finder. If Resurf disappeared tomorrow your library would still be sitting there, readable. That hasn't changed and won't.

Notes in Resurf

## New ways to capture

Voice notes, transcribed on device. You talk, it writes it down, cleans it up, and titles it. Nothing is sent anywhere to make that happen.

Quotes, for a line worth keeping, with its attribution, without wrapping a whole note around it.
